draft.title: Point of view and voice
card: First person
The narrator is part of the story and says I or we. The reader sees events through one person's eyes, so it feels close and personal.
Second person
The writer speaks to you. It pulls the reader into the action, as if the reader is the one acting or being addressed.
Third person
The narrator stands outside the story and uses he, she, they or a name. It can feel more distant, though a writer can still stay close to one character's thoughts.
Voice
Voice is the personality a reader hears in the writing. It is built from diction (word choices), rhythm (the pace and length of sentences) and attitude (the feelings the writer shows).
draft.remember: Point of view is who tells the story. Voice is the personality you hear in how it is told.

a.q: Which sentence is written in the first person?
opts: I crept down the hall, my heart thudding
She crept down the hall, her heart thudding
You creep down the hall, your heart thudding
Tariq crept down the hall, his heart thudding
a.why: The word I shows a narrator who is part of the story. She and his, and the name Tariq, show a third person narrator standing outside. The word you addresses the reader, which is second person.
a.clue: Look for a narrator who says I.

b.q: A writer describes a school sports carnival in short, snappy sentences, slang and a cheeky, mocking attitude. What are these choices building?
opts: A distinct voice
A third person viewpoint
A second person viewpoint
A formal register
b.why: Slang (diction), short sentences (rhythm) and a cheeky attitude together build a voice. Voice is not the same as point of view: the passage could be in first or third person and still have this voice.
b.clue: Diction, rhythm and attitude work together to build this.

a.best: I crept down the hall, my heart thudding

problems.detail: Spotting a first-person sentence by the word 'I' is a Year 7 skill, too easy for Year 11. The clue 'Look for a narrator who says I' also hands over the answer outright.

a.q: A writer changes 'She crept down the hall' to 'You creep down the hall'. What is the main effect of this change?
opts: It places the reader inside the action as the one acting
It shows events through the narrator's own eyes
It puts more distance between the reader and events
It moves the narrator to stand outside the story
a.why: The change is to second person, which pulls the reader into the action as if they are the one acting. Seeing events through the narrator's own eyes is the effect of first person, where the narrator says I, not you.
a.clue: Think about where the change puts the reader.
